note: Description of the game of this mod (spec: documentation/mecaniques/flux-de-jeu.md). Steps 1 to 4 of the migration: the sequence of a game (phases, steps, transitions, events, runners) is run from this file by prototype/flow.js, as are the reinforcement purchases; the interface is still drawn by code. "stat" / "gainStat" are the statistics of the end screen that it counts.

stats.note: Counters of the end screen; the resources with a "stat" feed them.

roles.note: The roles that the resources and the zones play for the engine (zones: field = where the cards fight, reserve = where they wait): money = what purchases cost; level = the reinforcement level; progress = the progress toward the next level; turn = the number of the room. A mod names its resources as it likes and says here which one plays each role.

offer.title: ui.chooseCard
offer.note: modifiers: powers carried by servants on the board that change the offers. upgradeFirstOffer: one card of the first offer of the reinforcement is replaced by a card of the next rank (it does not stack). offTypeChance: the first card of an offer of the given kind has a chance (the "percentPer" field of the power, in percent, added up for all carriers) to be of a type absent from the team.

adaptation.note: After a combat, each surviving servant that has the power "who.power" (and the type "who.type") chooses among its options. "extraPower": a servant with this power gets one more choice per copy (it will not be offered again what the previous choice offered). "learnExcludes": powers that cannot be learned from another servant.

ui.note: animations: event -> animation. The engine notes cues (g.cues) when a power asks for one ("cue" in the action, or cueAmount/cueUid recorded by a stats action: statGranted); the interface plays the animation that the mod chose for the event.

sounds.note: Sounds of the mod: name -> file of the mod (a path under the mod folder, e.g. sounds/hit.ogg). A name with null has no file yet: it is silent. The effects play them with the sound primitive.

ui.effectsNote: Effects of the events (spec: documentation/mecaniques/evenements-et-effets.md): { on: event, phase: pre (before the impact of an attack) or impact (default), if: expression on the event, do: [ primitives ] }. Events of the same kind on a card in one frame are shown as one (their numbers add up).

effectGroups.note: Groups of effects the player can turn off (a rule names its group). explain: the effects that show why something happens (the card whose power acts pulses and names its trigger, a beam goes from it to what it changes).

ui.journalNote: The visual journal (spec: documentation/mecaniques/evenements-et-effets.md): how each kind of event reads. The first rule of an event that fits is used; an event with no rule is not shown. The power that caused the event is added at the end of the line (journal.cause) unless the rule says noCause.

cards.note: Atlas Wanderer draws its servants, heroes and equipment on frame pictures (frames/, kit V9). The servant frame had its three painted sockets removed so that the sockets follow the data, and all the frames were lengthened in their text panel to the height of the former cards (ratio 1.65). Boxes are in percent of the card. See documentation/mecaniques/cartes.md.

companion.note: The companion card: handed to the player when a servant of "type" is recruited (once per game), it evolves during the game, does not count toward the hand limit, cannot be discarded or replaced and is lost for the game if it dies. Its name is nameFormat with {number} written in base numberBase on numberWidth digits; the number is the victories counted in the profile counter plus one.

fusion.note: Fusion: when the player has "count" identical servants (same name, none of them gold or fixed), board and hand together, they become one gold servant: the sum of their statistics, the sockets of the first, the powers with their values changed (the default rule below, or the "gold" field of the power's template), and no equipment (they go back to the hand, see rules.sockets.onFusion). Then the player picks a reward among cards of rank min(maxRank, level + rewardRankOffset). nameKey: text that names the gold servant ({name}).

heroActions.note: Active powers of the heroes (the "power" of a hero card with t = active names one of them). The player arms the button then clicks a servant of one of the zones that passes every test of "where". cost: resource, base and step (rules references) and what the step is multiplied by ("per": the number of times the hero used it); repeat: usable several times per reinforcement (otherwise once).

promises.note: Cards promised for later. The key is the fx of a hero power: when the event "on" (a step event of the flow) happens and a hero has that power, the player chooses one card among "choose.count" cards of the category "choose.category" and of rank "choose.rank" (exactly, if exactRank). The chosen card goes to the zone "deliver.to" as soon as "deliver.spent" units of the resource "deliver.resource" have been spent (it waits for a free slot if the zone is full). texts: the title of the choice ({rank}), the reminder of the delivery ({cost}), and the two log lines ({name}, {cost}).

bags.note: Bags of values drawn at random. Each bag holds every face "copies" times; a draw takes one at random without putting it back, and the bag is refilled when it is empty. The drawn value is added to the resource of "effect" (never below "floor"; gains count in the statistic of the resource). "animation": how the interface shows the draw (diceRoll needs exactly 6 faces). A power template draws from a bag with the action drawBag.

tokens.note: Kinds of units that powers summon (they are not cards of the catalogue). A summoned unit carries the id of its kind in its field token, so that powers can select it; its statistics start from the power's values plus the bonus of its carrier (summonA, summonH, from equipment) and the bonus of its side (summonBonus[kind], from powers), which can grow during the game.

triggers.note: The triggers of the powers (the `t` of a power on a card). Each has a kind for the display (combat or renfort: where its text is shown) and either a moment (a moment the engine announces and where it plays the powers: startCombat, space, assault, afterDamage, attackNoKill, attackSurvive, survive, deathrattle, allyDeath, enemyDeath, battlecry, startReinforcement, endReinforcement, active, passive) or an event (on) with who it concerns (who) and optionally a condition (if) and a limit (once): a derived trigger, played at the next safe point of the combat. A trigger with neither is a label: the power reacts through its template (reactions). Several names may share a moment. Spec: documentation/mecaniques/evenements-et-effets.md.

fatigue.note: Anti-stalemate rule: once the combat has lasted "start" attacks, all servants lose "increment" more HP at each turn (1, 2, 3…).

settlement.note: End of combat: each survivor of the winning side strikes the other side. Damage of a survivor = its rank x perRank + flat. The player's survivors strike the Boss; the Boss's survivors strike the player's heroes (one at a time: the only hero with the "taunt" keyword if there is exactly one, otherwise a random living one; a hero with the "absorb" keyword cancels the first hit it would take).

order.note: Resolution order of the start-of-combat effects. direction: leftToRight or rightToLeft inside a band. Powers can change bands, direction and replays through the event resolutionOrder, and the first attacker through the event firstSide (spec 12.3); the priority of a power is start.priority in its template. bands: who plays first (boss = the Boss's own power, opponent = the Boss's board, heroes = the player's heroes, ally = the player's board). replays: inBand = a side's replays right after its other effects; afterAll = all the replays after every other effect.

sockets.note: Equipment sockets. A servant has 0 to "max" sockets, each of a color from "colors" or the "wildcard" (accepts every color); an equipment has one color and goes in a free socket of the same color (preferred) or in a wildcard one; an uncolored equipment (token) fits any socket if "uncoloredFitsAny". When a servant is replaced (onReplace) or fused (onFusion), its equipment either goes back to the hand (returnToHand) or is lost (lose); each one breaks with probability "breakChance" and is lost.

reinforcement.note: Reinforcement purchases. "kinds": the kinds of reinforcement the player can buy (servant, equip), each with its cost in Datacrons; a kind that is absent cannot be bought (by the player or by the Boss). "proposals": number of cards offered per reinforcement level (index 0 = level 1; the last value is kept beyond the table).

game.note: Size and economy of a game. maxBoard / handMax: places on the board and in the hand. maxLevel: highest reinforcement level (also the highest rank offered by reinforcement); maxRank: highest rank (reached by fusion rewards). fusionRewardProposals: cards offered as a fusion reward. fusionCost / fusionStep: Datacron price of the active power that completes a fusion, and its increase after each use. prophecyCost: Datacrons to spend for the prophecy servant to come into play. levelCosts: contribution needed to go from level N to N+1, one number per level. income: Datacrons gained at each reinforcement by room number (the last value is kept beyond the table). bossBoards: one entry per board the Boss plays; malus = Datacrons fewer per room (1 = always one fewer, 0.5 = one fewer every other time). (The die of Datacrons is described in game.json, bags.) patchMax: the cybernetic patch gives X from 1 to patchMax, the value X being present (patchMax + 1 - X) times. gameTypes: number of types in play in a game (dungeon + heroes, completed at random); bossRandomTypes: types the Boss draws at random in addition to the three fixed ones of the dungeon.

miniBoss.note: The mini-boss: one fixed servant per Boss board, present from the first room and never replaced. It has one type (the one it represents) and the powers listed here (name: text miniBoss.name).

draw.note: Weight of a card in the draw of an offer: base + perSharedType x the number of its types that the team has (a servant has several types, an equipment one). Servants and equipment are drawn by their reinforcement kind.

strategies.note: Strategies of the Boss boards (spec: documentation/mecaniques/strategies.md). A strategy has a kind: parametric (the engine routine that buys servants, levels and equipment, tuned by want, level, equipP, score and target), board (the board is the plan of the room: rooms and growth) or random (built into the engine: any legal move). "default" is used by a dungeon that names none: a name, { use, override } or { pool: [names] } (drawn without repeating from board to board). Names and descriptions: texts behavior.<id> and behavior.<id>.desc. Behaviors of the Boss's boards (each game draws different ones, one per board). want: number of servants aimed for at a room, min(maxBoard, base + floor(room / per)); level: reinforcement level aimed for, base + floor(room / per); equipP: probability of buying an equipment rather than a servant once the board is full; score: how an offered card is valued (card = the engine's card score, rank = rank first, sharedTypes = card score + types shared with the board); target: which servant receives an equipment (strongest, leastEquipped, fixed = the mini-boss). Names and descriptions: texts behavior.<id> and behavior.<id>.desc.
